rounds.text: Minaxi Textiles is demonstrating a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a consistent five-year trend of increasing operating margins [E31]. This structural improvement is highlighted by a 15 percentage point expansion in operating margins over the last three years [E29] and a notable 12 percentage point increase in the most recent June 2026 quarter compared to the year-ago period [E30]. The company is actively deleveraging, successfully reducing total borrowings from Rs 14.34 Cr to Rs 12.20 Cr in the last year [E37]. Furthermore, management confidence is reflected in the steady accumulation of equity, with promoter holdings increasing to 38.80% [E39]. The business is also generating meaningful liquidity, evidenced by Rs 3.20 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E35]. Conceded: [E1], [E13], [E20], [E36], [E41], [E42], [E49], [E50], [E55], [E58], [E59].

The bull’s focus on margin expansion [E29, E30, E31] ignores the reality that the company’s profitability is collapsing, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months at -98% [E20] and a net profit decline of 95% year-over-year [E55]. While the bull highlights deleveraging [E37], the company remains heavily burdened with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.90x, meaning debt significantly exceeds net worth [E36]. The claim of liquidity is undermined by a cash conversion ratio of only 0.18x, indicating that reported profits are not being effectively translated into cash and suggesting potential issues with receivables [E33]. Furthermore, the promoter holding of 38.80% is explicitly flagged as a negative risk factor [E49], and the company’s long-term performance is defined by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -8% [E14] and a median return on equity of -58% over the last year [E28]. Conceded: [E29], [E30], [E31], [E35], [E37], [E39]. The stock is currently priced for 32% earnings growth [E43] despite a fundamental profile that has resulted in a -498% margin of safety [E42].
